https://www.politico.eu/article/pope-leo.text: PARIS — Pope Leo XIV urged France to embrace dialogue and diversity Friday, in a veiled swipe at populists as he arrived in Paris for a four-day visit. His appeal came seven months before France’s presidential election, with far-right candidate Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls for the National Rally and traditional parties struggling to hold voters after nearly a decade of Emmanuel Macron’s presidency. “A truly free society” prevents “authoritarian tendencies,” the pope said in a speech delivered alongside President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace. Advertisement Advertisement The pope named no politician or party. But his defense of diversity and religious freedom lands as Le Pen’s National Rally campaigns against immigration ahead of a presidential election she hopes to win for the first time. “This dialogue is all the more urgent in the context of present-day France, where the people of differing cultural and religious backgrounds are called to live together,” the pontiff continued. Standing in front of French government members and church dignitaries, the pope also argued against pushing religion out of public life, weeks after the National Rally said it was in favor of banning the Muslim headscarf. “Righteous secularism doesn’t mean excluding religion from public spaces,” he said. Macron said the pope brought “hope” to France and praised his work on artificial intelligence and human dignity. The papal visit will take Leo from the Élysée to UNESCO, Notre-Dame Cathedral and a youth vigil at the Stade de France. He will celebrate Mass on Saturday, expected to gather 600,000 people on the Champs-Elysées in Paris. French politics have become deeply polarized in recent years, with the far-right National Rally and the far-left France Unbowed gaining popularity, just as traditional parties struggle to attract voters after a decade of Macron’s presidency. Advertisement Advertisement According to Antonio Spadaro, undersecretary of the Vatican’s Dicastery for Culture and Education, the pontiff will not offer voting instructions while in France nor criticize those who want to vote for Le Pen. Those attracted to nationalism, he said, often have legitimate concerns about identity and “the fear of losing it” but have been “offered the wrong answer.” “The pope will not tell the French to be less French,” said Spadaro in an interview with POLITICO ahead of the visit. “Roots are a good thing. The trouble begins when roots are used as walls.”

Photograph: PR HANDOUT Queensland Queensland man charged with murder after three-month-old son dies from ‘significant internal injuries’ Uneeb Ullah, 28, from Ipswich, has been remanded in custody after his arrest on Tuesday evening for the alleged murder of the child Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Ben Smee Wed 7 Oct 2026 01.39 EDT Last modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 04.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Queensland man has been charged with the murder of his three-month-old baby son, after the boy died in hospital this week. The infant, from the Ipswich area west of Brisbane, died almost a week after being taken to hospital with “significant internal injuries”. The boy had been on life support. Uneeb Ullah, 28, was arrested on Tuesday evening and charged with the boy’s murder, which is designated a domestic violence offence. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email His matter was mentioned briefly in court on Wednesday but Ullah was not required to appear and did not enter a plea. Police said detectives from the Child Protection Investigation Unit launched an investigation on 1 October after the boy was taken to Ipswich hospital with significant injuries, and that the nature of those injuries prompted hospital staff to report the matter to police. He was later transferred to the Queensland children’s hospital. View image in fullscreen Police arrested Ullah on Tuesday evening. Photograph: PR HANDOUT Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, DI Michael Manago said the mother of the child was “extremely upset” and that both parents, who were born overseas, have limited support. The boy was the couple’s only child. “This is a terribly tragic event involving a very vulnerable young member of the community,” Det Insp. Manago said. “The boy’s mother is extremely upset as you can imagine; this is a terribly tragic event. “She is struggling, but we’re offering her all the support that we can through this very difficult time.” Police said they had spoken to the couple several times since they opened the investigation. The investigation would include looking at the “nature and dynamics” of the boy’s parents’ relationship. “It’s an incredibly confronting and difficult investigation,” Manago said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “We were conducting our investigation throughout the last number of days and gathering evidence. When Ullah’s case came before the court on Wednesday, police prosecutor Ben Messina asked it be stood down until later in the day. “I received a phone call this morning … that potentially more material would be provided and asked [that] this matter be stood down to the end of the list,” Messina said of the “relatively vague request”. The magistrate agreed to re-mention the case if other charges were laid. Kirstyn Nicholson, a Legal Aid solicitor representing Ullah, did not apply for bail and sought an adjournment. Ullah was remanded in custody until the matter returns to court on 26 October. – With AAP This story was amended on 7 October 2026.
